chunks: Ja’far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to us, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma’il ibn Muslim, from al-Sadiq Ja’far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:
Whoever sleeps exhausted from seeking lawful sustenance, sleeps forgiven.

key_terms.الحلال: The lawful, the permissible - referring to earning sustenance through legitimate means
key_terms.كالا: Exhausted, worn out - describing the state of physical fatigue from hard work
key_terms.مغفورا: Forgiven - indicating divine pardon and mercy

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for seeking halal sustenance in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) teaches that those who exhaust themselves earning a lawful livelihood are rewarded with divine forgiveness. This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Imams, reflects the Islamic emphasis on earning one’s sustenance through permissible means as an act of worship. In the context of early Islamic society where many faced the temptation of easier but forbidden gains, this saying affirmed the spiritual merit of honest labor.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. `ali b. al-Hasan b. `Ali b. `Abdullah b. al-Mughira al-Kufi (ra) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan b. `Ali narrated to us from his grandfather `Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma`il b. Muslim from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
Whoever sleeps out of exhaustion from seeking the halal, he sleeps forgiven.
